notice: Source-linked factual reference observations. No universal human enzyme weights. Reference-substrate kinetics and plasma-library boundary counts have different endpoints and must not be pooled as rate measurements.

kinetic_reference.source_location: Abid et al. 2009, Table 1 and kinetic-parameter methods

context.buffer: Tris-HCl; added manganese; see source for mixing volumes
context.substrate_chemistry: Mono-oxygenated NPY forms; peptide was oxidized with hydrogen peroxide before digestion. These are not unmodified free vaccine peptides.
context.rate_units: Vmax: pmol product / minute / microliter serum; Km: micromolar
context.limitations: Apparent product-specific kinetics in the reported assay. Other products were observed but lack corresponding calibrated rate constants. Km and Vmax are point estimates; no calibrated uncertainty distribution is supplied. No generic aminopeptidase-P isoform is assigned.

plasma_library.source_location: Maffioli et al. 2020, Table S1, Cleavage Sites worksheet
plasma_library.matrix: Pooled plasma from six pigs, approximately 50-fold dilution
plasma_library.substrate_chemistry: Synthetic library; no cysteine or methionine; norleucine included. Worksheet M denotes norleucine, not methionine.
plasma_library.limitations: Counts describe unique observed boundary contexts, not numbers of molecular cut events, enzyme abundance, probabilities, or absolute rates. The Filtered worksheet has 114 qualifying product rows; the source Cleavage Sites worksheet has 113 contexts. More distant boundaries can reflect successive terminal trimming. No selective enzyme-inhibitor panel identifies the enzymes. Dilution, sample preservation, species and library chemistry limit transfer. Missing boundaries are not validated negatives.

human_plasma_product_shares.source_location: Kuoppala et al. 2000, abstract and concentration-dependence results
human_plasma_product_shares.matrix: Dalteparin-anticoagulated human plasma diluted in assay buffer
human_plasma_product_shares.limitations: Product-pathway shares for bradykinin under these assay conditions. Not universal enzyme hazard weights, not a vaccine half-life, and not independent estimates that can be averaged with the NPY assay.
